introduction: On this Sunday, the servant of the Lord is called to be a light to the nations. In the Gospel, John the Baptist sees Jesus coming and says, Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world. He testifies that he saw the Spirit come down and remain on him. Paul greets the Church of God at Corinth, called to be holy. Let us follow the Lamb of God.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lamb of God takes away the sin of the world. Let us bring our prayers to the Father.
intentions: For the Church: that she may be a light to the nations, pointing to Christ as John the Baptist did. Let us pray to the Lord.
For Christian unity: that all who call on the name of the Lord Jesus may grow together in holiness. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those burdened by sin and guilt: that they may find freedom in the Lamb of God. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are discerning their path in life: that they may say to God, Here I am, I come to do your will. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may bear witness to Jesus in our daily lives. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, you sent your Son as the Lamb who takes away the sin of the world. Make us his witnesses, and a light to all the nations. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Behold the Lamb of God
reflection.body:
The servant in Isaiah's prophecy receives a mission bigger than he expected. Bringing Israel back to God is not enough: "It is too light a thing that you should be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob." God says, "I will also give you as a light to the nations, that you may be my salvation to the end of the earth." God's plan has always included everyone.

The psalm gives the servant's answer, words the Letter to the Hebrews later places on the lips of Christ: "Behold, I have come." And: "I delight to do your will, my God."

In the Gospel, John the Baptist sees Jesus coming toward him and cries out: "Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!" A lamb was the animal of Passover and of sacrifice. John is announcing who Jesus is and what he has come to do: to take away sin by giving himself. At every Mass, before Communion, the priest shows us the Host with words drawn from John's.

John also tells us how he recognized Jesus: "I have seen the Spirit descending like a dove out of heaven, and it remained on him." And he concludes: "I have seen and have testified that this is the Son of God." John's whole life was a finger pointing to Jesus.

Paul opens his letter to the Corinthians by reminding them who they are: "those who are sanctified in Christ Jesus, called saints, with all who call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ in every place." Every Christian is called to holiness.

This week, at Mass, when the priest says behold the Lamb of God, look at the Host with faith. And, like John, point someone else toward Jesus by your words or your example.
